To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
A balanced pulse generator is described.

(1) a balanced pulse generator delivering balanced high repetitive pulses of 26V peak amplitude and pulse widths of less than 140 ps has been designed, (2) the pulse generator is based on a npn silicon transistor operating in an avalanching mode and a step recovery diodes, (3) the balanced pulses are intended for near-field UWB radars.
a balanced pulse generator delivering pulses of high voltage and high repetition rate has been developed.

the development of a pulse generator with high repetition rates for UWB radar systems, which is capable of generating pulses in the picosecon range with peak values of more than 25V.
the design of an efficient and compact balanced pulse generator with a high voltage amplitude and a short pulse width for near-field UWB applications.
a novel approach of generating balanced picosecond pulses for near field UWB radar applications.

the balanced pulse generator is suitable for near-field radar applications.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the balanced pulse generator is capable of delivering high repetitive balanced pulses of high voltage amplitudes and pulse widths in a picosecond region.

we have developed an UWB pulse source with a very high pulse repetition rate (up to 10MHz), which is capable to produce high amplitude (25V) and very short (140 ps) pulses with a very high signal to noise ratio (SNR > 40dB) and a low jitter (< 10ps).
we have successfully designed, constructed, and tested an ultra-wide-bandwidth (UWB) pulse generator with the pulse width of about 140 ps and the peak voltage of about 25V.

the balanced pulse generator is capable of generating balanced pulses with peak amplitude of 25V, pulse width of 140ps, and a rise time of 25ps.
